purpose: Takes the person to a destination or runs a small in-flow action from inside text, next to a field or on a card. It reads as text with an underline, never as a control with its own surface.

notFor.case: An action that needs its own surface or must stand out.
An icon-only action in a toolbar or row.

Default.visual: Ink of the variant: Content/link/default (brand), Content/secondary (neutral), Content/inverse, Status/success/content, Status/info/content or Status/critical/content; underline shown or hidden by the app.

Hover.visual: Brand ink moves to Content/link/hover, neutral to Content/primary; the underline is always shown, in the ink colour.

Pressed.visual: As Hover: Content/link/hover or Content/primary, underline always shown.

Visited.visual: Painted the same as Default; the Figma file has no visited role.

Focused.visual: A 2px edge inside and a 2px halo outside: Border/focus with Border/ring/default for brand; Border/strong with Border/subtle for neutral; Border/inverse with Surface/inverse-muted for inverse; the status border-strong and border roles for the status variants.

a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches it unless disabled; Enter follows it (native link).
notes: The label is the accessible name; an icon-only link needs an aria-label.
Disabled sets aria-disabled and tabindex -1 and swallows the click.
Hover and Pressed always show the underline, so the link is not told by colour alone there; at rest the underline can be turned off.

openQuestions: Visited: the file paints Visited like Default and real :visited paints nothing. Should visited links ever look different?
Underline off at rest: inside running copy a link without underline is told only by colour. Should the underline be forced on in body text?
Minimum hit area: the xs size is a 12px text line. Is 24px a promise TextLink must keep (padding), or is it exempt as inline text?
